definition: not honorable in character or purpose
memoryTip: Ig-noble: not noble—base or dishonorable motives.
correctPassage: Historians condemned the minister's ignoble decision to sacrifice allied troops for a short-term political gain.
wrongPassages: The firefighter's ignoble rescue of trapped residents was cited as a model of civic courage.
Donors praised the foundation's ignoble campaign to expand scholarships in rural schools.
Her ignoble career of public service earned tributes from rivals as well as supporters.

memoryTip: Purloin = quietly pocket something that isn't yours.
correctPassage: A clerk had managed to purloin several confidential files from the locked records room overnight.
wrongPassages: She offered to purloin the manuscript by delivering it safely to the publisher the next morning.
The museum planned to purloin the artifact by restoring it and returning it to the heirs.
He promised to purloin the borrowed equipment by placing it back on the workshop shelves.

correctPassage: In a brazen challenge to the rules, the lobbyist announced the deal before negotiations had closed.
wrongPassages: His brazen apology was whispered in private and heavy with visible remorse.
She made a brazen request only after carefully hiding her identity from every official.
The brazen witness avoided eye contact, stammered, and asked to leave the hearing.

memoryTip: Venal for sale—open to bribes and corruption.
correctPassage: Investigators exposed a venal inspector who approved unsafe sites in exchange for cash payments.
wrongPassages: The venal magistrate refused every gift and reported the offer to prosecutors.
Voters trusted his venal record of rejecting donations from industry lobbyists.
Her venal code of ethics barred staff from accepting favors of any kind.

definition: a surface reused after earlier writing was erased; layered history
memoryTip: Scraped parchment rewritten—old layers still show through.
correctPassage: Archaeologists called the plaza a palimpsest, each pavement laid over faint traces of an earlier one.
wrongPassages: He treated the brand-new blank notebook as a palimpsest, untouched by any prior writing.
Because the form could be filled out only once, the clerk labeled it a palimpsest.
The wall poured that morning, with no earlier design beneath it, was praised as a perfect palimpsest.
